item.title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Regio‐ and Stereoselective Three‐Component Difunctionalization of Alkynes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This review summarizes nickel-catalyzed three-component alkyne difunctionalization via two catalytic modes, namely single nickel catalysis and photoredox/nickel dual catalysis, and outlines their mechanistic features, substrate scope, and current limitations.


Nickel-catalyzed three-component difunctionalization of alkynes has emerged as a powerful strategy for the rapid construction of complex molecular architectures with high step and atom economy. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in alkyne difunctionalizations and categorizes them into two sections based on different catalytic modes: single nickel catalysis and photoredox/nickel dual catalysis. The single nickel catalysis exploits the intrinsic redox versatility of nickel in combination with judicious ligand design to afford high levels of regio- and stereocontrol and broad functional-group tolerance. In contrast, the photoredox/nickel dual catalytic system merges visible-light-driven single-electron transfer with nickel–mediated bond formation, enabling otherwise challenging radical-type difunctionalizations under mild, room-temperature conditions and without external reductants. The mechanistic features, substrate scope, and representative examples of each paradigm are critically discussed, with emphasis on their distinct advantages and complementarity. Finally, current limitations and prospects for future development are outlined.

item.title: Multienzyme Cascade Reactions: Compatibility, Cooperativity, and Control
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Multienzyme cascade reactions are sequences of telescoped biotransformations that avoid the isolation of intermediates and offer significant efficiency advantages over traditional multistep routes. This review article highlights recent examples of multienzyme cascades and explores how their success depends on the consideration of compatibility, cooperativity, and control aspects in process design.


Multienzyme cascades combine several biocatalytic reactions in a single synthetic operation without isolation of intermediates. Compared to traditional multistep sequences, they offer significant advantages in terms of time and resource efficiency, and they often enable overall transformations that would not be possible by performing the constituent steps independently of each other. In this review article, we highlight selected multienzyme cascades from the recent literature (mainly 2020–2025) and discuss their main benefits and challenges along three overarching themes: compatibility of the required chemical transformations and biocatalysts, cooperativity between enzymes that operate concurrently in the same vessel, and control over the final outcome of the complete reaction sequence. Cascade designs that account for these aspects have enabled the expedient synthesis of a broad range of relevant target compounds, including complex pharmaceutical drugs prepared on industrial scale.

item.title: Photocascade Catalysis: Access to Arene Endoperoxides as Singlet Oxygen Batteries Through Oxyfluoroalkylation and Photooxygenation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A visible light–driven photocascade merging photoredox oxyfluoroalkylation with oxygen sensitization via energy transfer enables the direct synthesis of functionalized arene endoperoxides from vinyl-substituted arenes. The resulting endoperoxides act as thermally triggered singlet oxygen donors, with the arene substitution pattern influencing their thermolysis rates.


The merger of different visible light–driven reactions in one-pot processes is a powerful strategy for constructing functionalized molecular architectures. In this context, photocascade reactions based on combinations of single-electron transfer processes (SET–SET), sequences initiated by energy transfer followed by a photoredox step (EnT–SET), and SET–EnT processes have flourished in the literature. However, current approaches involving EnT processes are largely limited to alkene isomerizations. Herein, we report a photocascade transformation that merges photoredox oxyfluoroalkylation with oxygen sensitization via triplet–triplet energy transfer. This strategy enables the formation of functionalized arene endoperoxides from vinyl-substituted naphthalenes and anthracenes. These endoperoxides subsequently serve as efficient sources of singlet oxygen upon thermolysis. Investigation of the substitution pattern highlights the critical role of functional groups borne by the arene framework.

item.title: A General Red‐Light Photocatalytic Platform for the Synthesis of Perfluoroalkyl Tellanes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The syntheses of perfluoroalkyl aryl(alkyl)tellanes have been achieved under red light-photocatalysis with commercially available perfluoroalkyl iodides in excellent yields. Mechanistic insights reveal a radical chain process that accounts for the high product yields obtained. The resulting perfluoroalkyl tellanes constitute versatile building blocks for future applications in organofluorine chemistry, radical chemistry, materials science, and molecular design.


Perfluoroalkyl tellanes (RF–Te–R) constitute a synthetically valuable yet underdeveloped class of organotellurium compounds, despite their potential in fluoroorganic chemistry and materials science. Herein, we disclose a general, efficient, and operationally simple photocatalytic strategy for their synthesis from readily available ditellanes and perfluoroalkyl iodides. The transformation is enabled by red-light irradiation in the presence of zinc phthalocyanine as an inexpensive and readily accessible photocatalyst, allowing the generation of perfluoroalkyl radicals under exceptionally mild conditions. This protocol exhibits broad substrate scope, accommodating a wide range of diaryl, heteroaryl, and dialkyl ditellanes, including sterically congested and biologically relevant scaffolds, and consistently delivers the corresponding perfluoroalkyl tellanes in high yields. Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping experiments, Stern–Volmer analysis, and quantum yield determination (Φ = 2.4), reveal a photoinitiated radical chain mechanism in which the inherent lability of the Te─Te bond plays a key role in facilitating efficient radical capture and propagation. By combining low-energy photochemical activation with the unique reactivity of tellurium-centered species, this work establishes a practical and scalable platform for C─Te bond formation and significantly expands the synthetic toolbox for accessing perfluoroalkyl tellanes.

item.title: Ball‐Milling‐Enabled Pd‐Catalyzed One‐Pot Cross‐Coupling of Aryl Thianthrenium Salts With In Situ Generated Reformatsky Enolates
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Mechanochemical ball milling enables a practical single-step one-pot palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of aryl thianthrenium salts with in situ generated Reformatsky-type zinc enolates. The protocol proceeds under ambient conditions, avoids inert-atmosphere handling, and gives diverse α-arylated esters and amides, including bioactive-molecule derivatives, in useful to high yields.


Mechanochemistry enables an efficient Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of aryl thianthrenium salts with in situ generated Reformatsky-type enolates. Ball milling plays a dual role by promoting both the activation of zinc to form Reformatsky-type organozinc enolates from α-halo esters and amides and their subsequent cross-coupling with solid aryl thianthrenium salts. This single-step one-pot protocol provides access to a broad range of α-arylated products in high yields within short reaction times. The mechanochemical process is performed under ambient conditions without requiring an inert atmosphere, highlighting its operational simplicity and practicality. Furthermore, the methodology is readily applicable to the late-stage functionalization of structurally complex bioactive molecules.

item.title: Multicomponent Reactions Enabled by Photoinduced Formal Alkyl Transfer of Tertiary Amines
item.description: Multicomponent reactions (MCRs) provide a powerful and efficient strategy for rapidly accessing structurally diverse compounds under mild conditions. Among MCRs, the Ugi-type reactions—including the Ugi–azide variant—hold a central role in the synthesis of α-amino derivatives. Historically, research in this area has largely focused on expanding the scope of nucleophiles to access novel and complex products. However, most reported transformations still rely on imine (or iminium) intermediates generated from primary/secondary amines and aldehydes/ketones. In this work, we disclose a photochemical approach that utilizes photoexcited aromatic amines to trigger the oxidation of tertiary amines, leading to the formation of iminium species. These intermediates undergo a formal alkyl transfer process with aromatic amines to generate new iminium salts, which subsequently engage with various nucleophiles in a multicomponent fashion. This strategy enables the efficient synthesis of three important classes of functional molecules—α-amino phosphine oxides, tetrazoles, and imides—via a tertiary amine-involved MCR under light irradiation.

item.title: Transition‐Metal‐Free Mechanochemical Construction of C─P Bonds Using Diazonium Salts With H‐Phosphonates and Phosphine Oxides
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A transition-metal-free mechanochemical method for C─P bond formation is developed. Aryldiazonium salts react with bench-stable P(O)─H compounds under solvent-free ball-milling at room temperature via an ionic pathway. The protocol affords arylphosphonates and arylphosphine oxides in up to 96% yield with broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and excellent functional group tolerance.


A transition-metal-free mechanochemical protocol for the construction of C─P bonds is reported. The reaction employs aryldiazonium tetrafluoroborates and bench-stable P(O)─H compounds (H-phosphonates and phosphine oxides) under solvent-free ball-milling conditions at room temperature. In contrast to a previously reported radical-based mechanochemical C─P coupling utilizing stoichiometric magnesium and phosphoryl chlorides, our method operates via an ionic nucleophilic substitution pathway, as supported by the lack of inhibition by TEMPO and 1,1-diphenylethylene and the accelerating effect of electron-donating substituents. The protocol displays a broad substrate scope (43 examples, up to 96% yield), excellent functional group tolerance, and gram-scale applicability, providing a practical and sustainable route to arylphosphonates and arylphosphine oxides.

item.title: Photoinduced Synthesis of (Z)‐β‐Sulfonamido Enamines via an Electron Donor–Acceptor Complex With N‐(Sulfon)amido Pyridinium Salts
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A visible-light-induced, transition-metal, and photocatalyst-free methodology has been developed for the highly regio- and stereoselective C(sp2)–H amination of enamines with N-aminopyridinium salts via an electron donor–acceptor complex under mild conditions. This protocol provides straightforward access to diverse (Z)-β-sulfonamido enamines (32 examples, 31%–78% yield). Its synthetic utility is demonstrated through a gram-scale reaction, one-pot three-component processes, natural sunlight-driven transformations, and late-stage functionalization of drug derivatives.


A novel, visible-light-driven, transition-metal, and photocatalyst-free methodology for the C(sp2)–H amination of enamines has been developed, enabling the regio- and stereoselective synthesis of (Z)-β-sulfonamido enamines from readily accessible N-aminopyridinium salts. This new protocol provides straightforward access to a broad range of (Z)-β-sulfonamido enamines (32 examples, 31%–78% yields) and proceeds via an electron donor–acceptor complex-initiated radical pathway, as supported by mechanistic studies. Its synthetic robustness was further demonstrated through a gram-scale reaction, one-pot three-component processes, and successful application to natural sunlight-driven transformations. The utility of this method in pharmaceutical chemistry was highlighted by the late-stage functionalization of amino-containing drug derivatives. Overall, this operationally simple and mild strategy offers an efficient new platform for constructing functionalized enamine derivatives of synthetic significance.

item.title: Para‐Selective C─H Amination of Benzenepropanamides via Photocatalytic N‐Centered Radical‐Mediated Dearomatization
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A photocatalytic para-selective C─H amination of arenes using oxime-ester dual-radical precursors is described. N-centered radical dearomatization is proposed to generate cyclohexadienyl radical intermediates, which are proposed to undergo intermolecular radical–radical cross-coupling followed by base-promoted deprotonative rearomatization. This mild protocol tolerates a range of functional groups and affords para-aminated products with high site.


We report a photocatalytic strategy for constructing para-aminobenzenepropanamide scaffolds. This method employs oxime-ester-based diamination reagents as dual-radical precursors to generate imino and amidyl radicals. The key step involves N-centered radical-mediated intramolecular dearomatization, forming the cyclohexadienyl radical (CHDR) intermediate. This protocol features mild reaction conditions and broad functional group tolerance. Furthermore, this method achieves selectivity that is not affected by the stereochemical or electronic properties of the benzene ring, thereby enabling the efficient synthesis of 4-aminobenzoylamide.

item.title: Boosting Co‐Catalyzed [2+2+2]‐Cyclotrimerizations Through Strong π‐Acceptor Ligands
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

α-Cationic phosphine ligands dramatically enhance homogeneous Co-catalyzed [2+2+2] cyclotrimerization of alkynes. Their strong π-acceptor character increases metal electrophilicity, enabling rapid reactions at room temperature with low catalyst loadings. This approach unlocks efficient intermolecular trimerizations, overcoming the limitations of conventional cobalt systems and exemplifying the potential gain for 3d metal catalysis of these unique ligands.


α-Cationic phosphine ligands are strong π-acceptors that significantly enhance the electrophilicity of transition-metal centers. Herein, we demonstrate their effectiveness in cobalt-catalyzed [2+2+2] cyclotrimerization of alkynes, enabling the efficient synthesis of trisubstituted benzenes under mild conditions. The use of these ligands leads to a marked increase in catalytic activity, allowing reactions to proceed at room temperature and with catalyst loadings as low as 2 mol%. Results obtained with two different α-cationic phosphines, cyclopropenio- and pyridiniophosphine, suggest that enhanced π-backdonation to the α-cationic phosphine increases the electrophilicity of the cobalt center, thereby promoting cyclization. The methodology displays broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, including challenging sterically hindered alkynes. These results highlight the potential of α-cationic phosphines to boost the performance of earth-abundant metal catalysts and advance sustainable catalytic strategies.

item.title: Influence of Supports on Electrocatalytic Performance of Dual‐Atom Catalysts
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This review summarizes the influence of supports in dual-atom catalysts for electrocatalysis, discussing the carrier categorization, structure design, modulation strategies, dynamic evolution of diatomic sites during the electrocatalytic processes, and the applications in electrocatalysis and energy conversion devices.


Due to excellent atomic usage, stability, activity, and selectivity, dual-atom catalysts (DACs) have attracted a lot of attention in electrocatalysis. The dispersion, electrical structure, stability, and catalytic reaction dynamics of the functional sites are all directly influenced by the chemical and physical properties of the supports, including specific surface area, pore structure, conductivity, and surface chemical state. Here, the support categorization and structure design of DACs are examined. To expedite the development of high-performance DACs and uncover the structure–performance relationship, a sensible modulation technique is subsequently put out. Furthermore, the dynamic evolution of diatomic sites during the electrocatalytic processes is demonstrated using sophisticated characterization techniques. Afterward, the applications of DACs in energy conversion devices and electrocatalysis are examined. Finally, the potential and problems associated with the continued development of DACs for energy-related applications are presented.

item.title: Photoelectrochemically Driven Hydrophosphorylation of Alkynes to Access (E)‐Alkenylphosphine Oxides
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

An effective photoelectrocatalysis has been established for the hydrophosphorylation of diaryl acetylenes, a transformation that cannot be achieved by either photoredox catalysis or electrocatalysis when used separately. This protocol reversed stereoselectivity relative to radical-based protocols and delivered products with exclusive E-selectivity. Crucially, this method effectively prevents undesired over-reduction, specifically double hydrophosphorylation of alkynes.


The current metal-free methods for the hydrophosphorylation of alkynes, encompassing both electrochemical-driven and photoredox-catalyzed processes separately, show efficacy only when applied to less hindered terminal alkynes, polarized internal alkynes, or aryl alkyl internal alkynes; diaryl acetylenes are found to be incompatible with these conditions. Both methods involve a radical stepwise addition, yielding a Z/E isomeric mixture with the Z-alkenylphosphine oxides as the primary products. Furthermore, electrochemical hydrophosphorylation of alkynes is prone to double reduction of alkynes during extended reaction times. Herein, in sharp contrast to conventional, often separate, electrochemical or photoredox catalytic approaches that typically produce a Z/E isomeric mixture, this photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) process, which combines photocatalysis and electrochemistry, exclusively furnishes stereospecific (E)-alkenylphosphine oxides as the sole products. Significantly, this protocol successfully applies efficiently to diaryl acetylenes and bulky terminal alkynes, with no iterative addition of triple bonds observed.

item.title: Advances in the Phosphorus Functionalization Reactions of Stable Enamines
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Herein, the research advances in the phosphorus functionalization reactions of stable enamines, including enaminones, enaminoesters, cyanoenamine, enamides, etc., are presented. The review shows the application of these functionalization reactions involving direct C–H functionalization, π-bond functionalization, C─N bond funtionalization, C═C double-bond cleavage, and cascade annulation reactions in the synthesis of highly divergent organophosphorus compounds. The contents provide useful guidelines to the synthesis and potential application in the discovery of useful phosphorus compounds and related organic materials with enamine-based reactions.


Enamines are well known for their highly versatile and distinctive reactivity toward the generation of molecular diversity and complexity. By reacting with phosphorus-based reagents, enamines are able to generate a broad array of phosphorus containing organic products, providing practical accesses to structurally diverse phosphorus-functionalized small molecules through different reaction pathways. Herein, based on our longstanding interest and the recent advances in this area, the advances in the phosphorus functionalization of stable enamines are reviewed. According to the feature of the key transformations, the reactions based on the vinyl C–H functionalization, π-bond functionalization, the cascade cyclization reaction, and other related reactions are introduced and discussed individually.

item.title: Application of Bifunctional Togni’s Reagent in Photoredox‐Catalyzed Oxytrifluoromethylation of Alkenes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

We report a photoredox-catalyzed oxytrifluoromethylation of alkenes with Togni’s reagent, which efficiently affords diverse CF3-containing esters, enables late-stage functionalization of drug molecules under mild conditions, and permits conversion into other valuable building blocks. This method employs Togni’s reagent as both the trifluoromethyl and acyloxy source, enabling external nucleophile-free difunctionalization with high atom economy.


We report a radical-based protocol for the photoredox-catalyzed oxytrifluoromethylation of alkenes with Togni’s reagent. This strategy provides efficient access to a broad array of CF3-containing esters and is also applicable to late-stage functionalization of drug molecules under mild conditions. Moreover, conversion of the resulting CF3-functionalized esters to other valuable building blocks is also achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that Togni’s reagent acts as both a trifluoromethyl and an acyloxy group. Consequently, the difunctionalization reaction can proceed without any external nucleophiles, offering high atom economy.

item.title: Interfacial Co–Ni Dual‐Site Synergy in Confined Co9S8–Ni3S2 Heterostructures for Electrocatalytic Water Splitting
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Co9S8–Ni3S2 heterostructures confined in nitrogen-rich spongy carbons trigger interfacial Co–Ni dual-site synergy and dynamic electrochemical self-reconstruction, thus promoting efficient water activation and delivering outstanding bifunctional electrocatalytic performance for alkaline water splitting.


Although heazlewoodite-type nickel sulfide (Ni3S2) exhibits promising hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, its application in overall water splitting remains limited by sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics associated with insufficient water activation. Herein, Co9S8–Ni3S2 heterostructures confined in nitrogen-rich spongy carbons are constructed to regulate interfacial electronic properties and unlock Co–Ni catalytic synergy for efficient water electrolysis. A melamine sponge is employed as a 3D scaffold to direct the spatial anchoring of Co2+ and Ni2+ precursors, followed by in situ sulfidation and carbonization to form a conductive porous carbon framework with confined sulfide heterointerfaces. The resulting heterointerfaces trigger significant spin polarization and electron redistribution from Ni3S2 to Co9S8 through interfacial Co–S–Ni configurations, thus activating the Co–Ni dual sites for enhanced water adsorption and dissociation. The catalyst exhibits outstanding bifunctional OER/HER activity and long-term stability in alkaline media, while an alkaline electrolyzer assembled with the catalyst requires only 1.515 V to deliver 10 mA cm−2. Moreover, in situ and ex situ analyses reveal dynamic reconstruction of the Co–Ni sites under OER conditions, continuously generating additional active centers and sustaining high catalytic activity. This work paves a new way for designing earth-abundant and high-performance heterostructured electrocatalysts toward green hydrogen production.

item.title: Mild Generation of Vinyl, Methyl, Heteroaryl, and Cyclopropyl Radicals From Boronic Esters via Photoinduced Deboronation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

We demonstrated a mild and efficient approach for the generation of unstabilized radicals such as vinyl, methyl, heteroaryl, and cyclopropyl radicals from the corresponding easy-to-handle boronic esters to enable C─C bond formation with alkenes in a two-molecule photoredox system without transition metals.


The photoinduced deboronative generation of unstabilized radicals, including vinyl, methyl, heteroaryl, and cyclopropyl radicals, from commercially available and easy-to-handle boronic esters under mild conditions in a two-molecule photoredox system was achieved. The generated unstabilized radicals readily added to electron-deficient alkenes, resulting in new C─C bond formation without transition metals.

item.title: Iodanyl Radical Catalysis Enables Ring‐Opening and δ‐C─H Functionalization of Aliphatic Alcohols
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A simple monodentate aryl iodide, 2-iodopyridine, operates as an efficient organo-iodine catalyst in photocatalytic I(I)/I(II) iodanyl radical catalysis. Integrated with visible-light photoredox catalysis, this metal-free system enables single-electron activation of unfunctionalized aliphatic alcohols to generate alkoxy radicals. This dual manifold achieves both ring-opening functionalization of cyclic alcohols and site-selective δ-C(sp3)─H functionalization via 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer.


Iodanyl radical catalysis offers distinct reactivity beyond conventional two-electron hypervalent iodine manifolds. However, existing catalytic protocols rely predominantly on complex bis-iodoarene platforms to stabilize radical intermediates, whereas simple monodentate aryl iodides remain poorly developed due to off-cycle pathways. Herein, we report that 2-iodopyridine serves as a highly efficient organo-iodine catalyst for photocatalytic iodanyl radical catalysis under mild, redox-neutral, and metal-free conditions. Integrated within a visible-light photoredox cycle, this protocol achieves direct single-electron activation of unfunctionalized aliphatic alcohols to generate reactive alkoxy radical intermediates. This dual catalytic manifold facilitates both ring-opening functionalization of cyclic alcohols via β-scission and site-selective δ-C─H functionalization of linear alcohols through 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer. Mechanistic investigations and radical trapping experiments support the proposed one-electron catalytic pathway. This strategy provides an accessible and low-cost platform for iodanyl radical catalysis, expanding the synthetic utility of native aliphatic alcohols.

item.title: Redox‐Neutral C(sp3)─H Alkenylation via Photocatalyzed Tandem Hydrogen Atom Transfer and Downstream Oxidative Radical Polar Crossover
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Herein, we present a photocatalytic route exploiting a redox-neutral tandem hydrogen atom transfer and oxidative radical polar crossover manifold. This method enables the synthesis of allylic amides and ethers from feedstock chemicals, showing broad functional group tolerance, mild conditions, and efficient scalability.


Herein, we present a photocatalytic route that exploits a redox-neutral tandem hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and oxidative radical polar crossover (RPC) manifold. This method enables the efficient synthesis of valuable allylic amides and ethers through the valorization of three classes of ubiquitous feedstock chemicals: carboxylic acids as precursors to hydrogen atom abstractors, amides or ethers as C(sp3)─H donors, and olefins as radical acceptors. The protocol operates under mild conditions, exhibits broad functional group tolerance, and is readily scalable. The redox-neutral nature of this transformation mechanistically distinguishes it from traditional net-oxidative approaches associated with exogenous stoichiometric oxidants. Crucially, it allows HAT substrates bearing “hydridic” C─H bonds (e.g., α- to heteroatom: X─CHR1R2) to be engaged in Giese-type addition reactions and subsequent oxidative RPC/nucleophilic trapping, where traditional net-oxidative approaches inevitably result in Shono-type further oxidation of the HAT-derived radical (e.g., α- to heteroatom: X+═CR1R2) and nucleophilic interception prior to intermolecular radical addition.

item.title: Photochemical Efficient Radical Normalized Transformation of N‐nitrosamines Triggered by Energy Transfer Process
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

We report a photochemical energy‑transfer strategy that converts diverse N‑nitrosamines into perfluoroalkyl oximes (up to 99% yield) via reaction with alkenes and perfluoroalkyl iodides. The protocol exhibits broad functional‑group tolerance, ideal for late‑stage modification of complex molecules. It also proves useful for N‑nitrosamine impurity analysis, with validation using irbesartan batches confirming robust quantification for pharmaceutical quality control.


N‑nitrosamines are potent carcinogenic contaminants widely present in food, pharmaceutical products, and environmental matrices, posing considerable risks to human health. The accurate detection of these compounds calls for the urgent development of an efficient and chemoselective transformation capable of converting diverse N‑nitrosamines into a single, stable product. Herein, we report a photochemical radical normalization strategy that achieves this goal via an energy‑transfer process. This methodology enables the synthesis of structurally diverse perfluoroalkyl oximes from N‑nitrosamines, alkenes, and perfluoroalkyl iodides with up to 99% yields. The protocol exhibits broad functional‑group tolerance, rendering it particularly attractive for the late‑stage functionalization of complex molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that energy transfer from photoexcited N‑nitrosamines to perfluoroalkyl iodides concurrently suppresses undesired amino radical formation and promotes perfluoroalkyl radical generation, ensuring high reaction selectivity. Furthermore, this strategy proves applicable to the analysis of various N‑nitrosamine impurities. Validation experiments using irbesartan active pharmaceutical ingredient batches confirmed the robust quantification of total N‑nitrosamine content, demonstrating its practical utility in pharmaceutical quality control.

item.title: Front Cover: Mild Generation of Vinyl, Methyl, Heteroaryl, and Cyclopropyl Radicals From Boronic Esters via Photoinduced Deboronation (Adv. Synth. Catal. 21/2026)
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Photoinduced Deboronation

The photoinduced deboronative generation of unstabilized radicals, including vinyl, methyl, heteroaryl, and cyclopropyl radicals, from commercially available and easy-to-handle boronic esters under mild conditions in a two-molecule photoredox system was achieved. The generated unstabilized radicals readily added to electron-deficient alkenes, resulting in new C−C bond formation without transition metals. item.title: Radical Strategies to Activate Organoboron Reagents for Cross‐Coupling Reactions
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Halogen atom radicals activate organoboron compounds to generate carbon radicals, providing several advantages. These carbon radicals can subsequently participate in various reactions, including Suzuki–Miyaura reaction, the Chan–Lam reaction, Giese addition, Michael addition, the Minisci reaction, alkylarylation of alkenes, alkylation and nitrosoalkylation of N-heteroaromatics, three-component alkylarylation of alkenes, and enantioconvergent deborylative C(sp3)–C(sp) coupling of racemic boronic esters with alkynes.


In organic synthesis, organoboron reagents—especially alkylboronic acids and their pinacol esters (APEs)—have attracted significant attention due to their advantages, including low toxicity, ease of handling, and bench stability. Therefore, they are considered attractive alternatives as radical sources. However, it is quite challenging to generate these carbon radicals directly from boron compounds because of their high oxidation potentials and low Lewis acidity. This minireview focuses on recent advances in this area, in which heteroatom radicals are applied to activate boron compounds to generate carbon radicals. The review is organized according to activation mechanisms: bromine radical-mediated activation, oxygen radical-mediated processes, nitrogen radical (aminyl radical) transfer strategies, direct photoexcitation of synthesized borate complexes, and other approaches, including triplet–triplet energy transfer, electron donor–acceptor complex formation, and catechol-mediated thermal initiation. For each of these approaches, we discuss the underlying mechanism, substrate scope, synthetic utility, current limitations, and future development.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Promoted Radical Tetrafluoroethylation/Cyclization of N‐Alkenyl Indoles: Access to Tetrafluoroethylated Pyrrolo[1,2‐a]indoles
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

We herein report a visible-light-promoted radical cascade cyclization of N-alkenyl indoles with 1,2-dibromotetrafluoroethane (BrCF2CF2Br), affording tetrafluoroethylated pyrrolo[1,2-a]indoles in up to 95% isolated yield. The mild and operationally simple reaction exhibits broad functional-group tolerance.


Tetrafluoroethylated motifs are increasingly widespread in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, efficient and sustainable methods for their incorporation into complex polycyclic frameworks remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a visible-light-promoted radical cascade cyclization of N-alkenyl indoles using readily available 1,2-dibromotetrafluoroethane (BrCF2CF2Br) as a tetrafluoroethyl radical source. This mild protocol enables a facile one-step construction of tetrafluoroethylated pyrrolo[1,2-a]indoles bearing a quaternary carbon center. The reaction exhibits broad functional group tolerance, delivering the desired products in up to 95% isolated yield. Mechanistic studies support a photoredox radical cascade pathway. This work offers a sustainable and operationally simple approach to pharmaceutically relevant fluorinated polycyclic indoles from easily accessible starting materials.

item.title: Selective Catalytic Oxidation of Glycerol to 1,3‐Dihydroxyacetone Over Supported Au/CuO–SnO2 Catalysts: The Influence of Support Preparation Methods
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

In heterogeneous catalysis, the relationship between structure and performance is a long-standing core issue, which is about how to enhance catalytic performance by adjusting the structure. In this work, four different morphology CuO–SnO2 composite oxides were synthesized. And then Au nanoparticles were immobilized on above supports. The influence of the support structure on the catalytic glycerol oxidation by the supported Au catalysts has been verified.


This study investigates how interactions within catalysts impact performance in catalytic oxidation systems. In this work, a series of Cu-doped SnO2 supports with different morphologies are synthesized via sacrificial template, hydrothermal, solvothermal, and coprecipitation methods, respectively. And then Au nanoparticles were supported onto the above four supportsthrough urea deposition to obtain Au/CS-HT, Au/CS-NS, Au/CS-YS, and Au/CS-DP catalysts. Under mild conditions, the Au/CS-HT catalystexhibited optimal catalytic performance for the conversion of glycerol to 1,3-dihydroxyacetone (DHA). Glycerol conversion and DHA selectivity reached 62.2% and 81.2%, respectively. Characterization revealed that the sacrificial-template catalyst’s strong component interactions yield unique crystalline properties: uniformly distributed Cu2+ ions and abundant oxygen vacancies in SnO2 enhance oxygen activation, while Au-support electronic synergistic effect and appropriate basic sites selectively oxidize secondary hydroxyl groups in glycerol. These findings provide new design principles for optimizing metal–support interactions through synthesis methods of support.

item.title: Photoredox‐Catalyzed Strain‐Release Annulation of N‐Cyclopropylamides With Diazenes
item.description: Pyrazolidines are valuable saturated N–N heterocycles, yet convergent routes from independently variable C3 and N2 components remain limited, particularly when mono-donor cyclopropanes are employed as C3 synthons. Herein, we report a visible-light photoredox-catalyzed strain-release annulation of mono-donor N-cyclopropylamides with diazenes. The transformation integrates single-electron-transfer oxidation of N-cyclopropylamides with strain-driven cleavage of an otherwise electronically unbiased C─C σ bond and dual C─N bond formation, providing direct access to 3-amidopyrazolidines bearing a cyclic N-acyl aminal motif. A broad range of aryl, heteroaryl, aliphatic, and drug-derived N-cyclopropylamides, together with azodicarboxylates, diaryl diazenes, azodicarboxamides, and a cyclic azo reagent, are compatible under mild, metal-free conditions. Preliminary reactions with N-sulfinylamines and an N-cyclobutylamide furnish five- and six-membered N,S-heterocycles, suggesting that this photoredox platform may be applicable to other heteroatom–heteroatom π components.

item.title: Cu‐ERI Zeolite Catalysts With Tailored Properties for the Removal of N‐Containing Compounds
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The study found that Cu-ERI zeolites, especially Cu-ERI_2, show strong low-temperature NH3-SCR-DeNO x activity and high N2 selectivity because they contain highly active, easily reducible Cu2+ species; Cu-ERI_2 also facilitates NH3 activation and preferentially consumes NH3 adsorbed on Brønsted acid sites during NO reduction.


A series of ERI-type zeolite materials of different properties was prepared, which led to the obtaining of Cu-containing ERI materials of distinct catalytic properties in the selective catalytic reduction of NO x with ammonia (NH3-SCR-DeNO x ) and the selective catalytic oxidation of ammonia (NH3-SCO). Various characterization techniques were employed to describe the copper species in the synthesized ERI zeolite in order to understand its NH3-SCR-DeNO x and NH3-SCO activity as well as N2 selectivity. Cu-ERI_1 and Cu-ERI_2 possess the highest amount of active sites (i.e., Cu2+ species) and thus enhanced activity in the low-temperature range of NH3-SCR-DeNO x (with NO conversion of 83%–93% and N2 selectivity of 93%–95% at 250 °C). Especially, Cu-ERI_2 possesses easily reducible Cu2+ species that are responsible for activation and oxidation of NH3. Indeed, steady-state isotopic transient kinetic analysis of NH3-SCO revealed the shortest average surface lifetime and the lowest surface concentration of NH3 over the Cu-ERI_2 sample. Further, modulation excitation experiments confirmed that NO preferentially consumes NH3 adsorbed on the Brønsted acid sites on this sample. For other samples, the experiments of NO absorption followed by NH3 + O2 exposure and around (NH3 adsorption and NO + O2 exposure) indicated that NH3 adsorbed on Lewis acid sites is preferentially consumed during the reaction process.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Triggered Hydroacylation of α‐Imino Esters With α‐Keto Esters via Substrate Self‐Catalysis
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A self-catalyzed photochemical hydroacylation of α-imino esters with α-keto esters uses the α-keto ester as acyl donor, visible-light absorber, and H-atom abstractor, avoiding any metal or photosensitizer. This mild method provides diverse α-ketoamides and concise access to pharmaceutically relevant motifs.


α-Ketoamides are important structural motifs in bioactive molecules. While conceptually efficient, direct acylation of imines toward α-ketoamides is hindered by their intrinsic instability and reactivity challenges. Here, we disclose a photochemical hydroacylation of α-imino esters with α-keto esters that operates without any transition metal or external photosensitizer. Mechanistic elucidation reveals that the α-keto ester plays a triple role: It serves as an unconventional hydroacylation donor, a visible-light absorber, and a hydrogen-atom abstractor, collectively enabling substrate-driven self-catalysis. This strategy provides rapid access to structurally diverse α-ketoamide derivatives (44 examples) with high yields (up to 97%) under mild, environmentally benign conditions. By integrating multifunctional substrates and self-catalytic photoreactivity, this approach expands the toolbox for constructing complex ketoacyl frameworks, offering a concise route toward pharmaceutically relevant motifs.

item.title: Synthesis of γ,γ‐Disubstituted γ‐Butyrolactones via Copper‐Catalyzed Arylation–Lactonization of γ,δ‐Unsaturated Esters With Diaryliodonium Salts
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A copper-catalyzed arylation–lactonization of γ,δ-unsaturated esters with diaryliodonium salts has been developed, offering an efficient route to γ,γ-disubstituted γ-butyrolactones. A variety of γ-substituted butyrolactones with electronically diverse aryl moieties are synthesized under mild conditions. A gram-scale reaction has been successfully performed, demonstrating the scalability of this method.


A Cu-catalyzed arylation–lactonization process of γ,δ-unsaturated esters using diaryliodonium salts as aryl sources is reported. Aryl units having an electron-donating or electron-withdrawing group are transferred successfully to the substrates, providing the corresponding γ,γ-disubstituted γ-butyrolactones under mild conditions with high efficiency. The potential scalability of this method is demonstrated by a successful gram-scale reaction at a 5.0 mmol scale. This approach offers a practical alternative to existing methods that employ precious metal catalysts or potentially explosive aryl sources.

item.title: Thiolane Sulfoximines as Azide Surrogates for Quinolyl Nitrenes: Photochemical Access to Ortho‐Diaminoquinolines
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Thiolane sulfoximines provide practical and safer surrogates for hazardous azides in nitrene photochemistry, enabling direct access to 7,8-diaminoquinolines and fused δ-lactams. DFT calculations support the reaction mechanism and rationalize product selectivity.


Quinolyl nitrenes are valuable reactive intermediates for the synthesis of nitrogen-containing heterocycles but are commonly generated from hazardous azides under photochemical conditions. Herein, we introduce quinolyl thiolane sulfoximines as practical and thermally stable precursors for the photochemical generation of 8-quinolyl nitrenes. Upon UV irradiation, these sulfoximines undergo selective S─N bond cleavage and react efficiently with primary and secondary amines, providing direct access to structurally diverse 7,8-diaminoquinolines in moderate to excellent yields. The transformation releases tetramethylene S-oxide as a small, benign, readily removable by-product and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance, including compatibility with amino acid derivatives, enabling the synthesis of valuable fused δ-lactam scaffolds. DFT calculations support a mechanism involving nitrene formation followed by azirine trapping and rationalize the experimentally observed selectivity between diaminoquinoline and aminoazepine products. Overall, this work establishes quinolyl sulfoximines as practical and safer surrogates for azides in nitrene photochemistry, providing an efficient platform for the synthesis of 7,8-diaminoquinolines.

item.title: Regioselective Diversification of Aminopyrazoles via Ir‐Catalyzed C─H Borylation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Aminopyrazoles, an important bioactive pharmacophore, are typically accessed inefficiently through de novo syntheses that yield isomeric mixtures of 3- and 5-substituted derivatives. To address this challenge, we have elaborated readily available 3- and 5-aminopyrazole fragments using Ir C─H borylation, regioselectively furnishing boronates for downstream functionalization, including Suzuki–Miyaura arylation and regiospecific isomerization.


Aminopyrazoles are privileged molecular cores in drug design that present unique synthetic challenges, particularly when developing direct, site-selective transition metal-catalyzed C─H functionalization. Specifically, differentiating between C─H sites while contending with the reactivity of the amine and azinyl components is an unresolved challenge. Here, we describe strategies for the regioselective functionalization of 3- and 5-aminopyrazoles through Ir-catalyzed C─H borylation, exploiting the interplay between intrinsic reactivities and directing effects that influence C─H activation. The resulting borylated adducts can readily be elaborated to provide a range of arylated aminopyrazoles. Collectively, these studies constitute a general and readily adaptable blueprint for selectively generating isomeric aminopyrazole pharmacophores with tunable product distributions.

item.title: Ciprofloxacin Hydrochloride‐Enhanced Potassium tert‐Butoxide‐Mediated Direct Pyrazinylation of (Hetero)aryl Halides
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

An inexpensive and readily available quinolone drug serves as an effective additive in the t-BuOK-mediated pyrazinylation of (hetero)aryl halides, particularly less reactive aryl chlorides. The protocol exhibits good functional-group compatibility, scalability and enables the late-stage modification of structurally complex pharmaceuticals, providing practical access to diverse aryl pyrazines.


Aryl pyrazines are increasingly prevalent in the fields of pharmaceuticals and luminescent materials. Base-promoted cross-coupling reactions of (hetero)aryl halides with pyrazines can effectively avoid the drawbacks of limited substrate sources in conventional condensation and the cost as well as toxicity issues of noble metal catalysts inherent in transition metal-catalyzed methods. However, existing methods are predominantly applicable to (hetero)aryl iodides and bromides, whereas the direct use of less reactive (hetero)aryl chlorides remains challenging. Herein, we report a ciprofloxacin hydrochloride with potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) catalytic system for the construction of aryl pyrazines. In this reaction, a variety of (hetero)aryl bromides and chlorides prove to be viable substrates and exhibit excellent compatibility with a variety of functional groups. The developed system allows the preparation of aryl pyrazines on a gram-scale and the functionalization of complex pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies reveal that a radical-mediated pathway is involved in this catalytic transformation.

item.title: Chemoselective Recognition of Vinyl Organometalloids in Cobalt‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A cobalt catalyst displays an unusual ability to recognize terminal vinylmetalloid motifs in the presence of other alkene functionalities. Hydrosilylation proceeds exclusively at vinyl groups attached to Si, Ge, or B, while allyl, aliphatic, internal, and substituted alkenes remain unreactive. The resulting selectivity enables controlled modification of multivinyl building blocks.


Achieving selective functionalization of vinylsilanes in the presence of other terminal C═C bonds remains a significant challenge in organosilicon chemistry. Here, we report a cobalt catalyst supported by a bidentate aminophosphine ligand that enables highly chemoselective hydrosilylation of terminal vinylmetalloids under mild, solvent-free conditions. The earth-abundant system operates without external activators, as the hydrosilane substrate itself promotes catalyst activation. Remarkably, reactivity is restricted to terminal vinylmetalloid motifs, encompassing vinylsilanes, vinylgermanes, and vinylboronates, whereas allylsilanes, terminal alkenes, internal alkenes, and 1,1-disubstituted derivatives remain unreactive. This unusual selectivity enables exclusive transformation of vinylmetalloid groups even in multifunctional substrates containing olefinic sites. Control of substrate stoichiometry further provides access to structurally diverse organosilicon products from multiple-vinyl precursors with high efficiency.

item.title: Late‐Stage Diversification of Carbazolyl‐Derived Phosphines via Ru(II)‐Catalyzed P(III)‐Directed C─H Alkenylation With Internal Alkynes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)


We report a ruthenium-catalyzed P(III)-directed ortho-C─H alkenylation of carbazolyl-derived phosphines with internal alkynes. The trivalent phosphorus atom serves as an efficient directing group, enabling the highly selective synthesis of monoalkenylated phosphines in moderate to good yields. By tuning the reaction conditions, the corresponding dialkenylated products can also be obtained in acceptable yields. This protocol provides a straightforward and versatile route to a diverse library of functionalized PhenCarPhos-type ligands. Notably, these ligands exhibit superior catalytic performance to common commercially available or unfunctionalized phosphines in the palladium-catalyzed amination of aryl chlorides with morpholine.

item.title: Pyridine‐2‐Sulfinate as a Bifunctional SO2 Transfer Reagent; Unlocking Structurally Diverse, Ortho‐Functionalized Masked Sulfinates
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The commercially available 2-pyridyl “Willis’ sulfinate” is demonstrated as an efficient SO2 transfer reagent (STR) providing single-step access to a 2-pyridyl masked sulfinate from (hetero)aryl bromides and iodides. Following installation, the pyridyl auxiliary delivers ortho-selective functionalization via chelate-assisted CH activation, providing a divergent route toward densely substituted ortho-functionalized masked sulfinates.


Masked sulfinates have emerged as versatile intermediates in sulfur(VI) chemistry. Although SO2-transfer reagents enable their direct installation onto arenes, their coupling to sterically hindered ortho-substituted aryl halides remains broadly inefficient. Herein, we report the commercially available sodium 2-pyridylsulfinate (2-SO2Py-Na) as a simple and efficient SO2-transfer reagent for installing the 2-pyridylsulfone (2-SO2Py) group onto aryl iodides and bromides. Rather than overcoming this limitation through direct coupling of ortho-substituted substrates, the 2-SO2Py auxiliary enables a complementary route to ortho-functionalized products through directed C─H functionalization prior to sulfinate release. This strategy provides modular access to ortho-substituted sulfonyl derivatives, including sulfonyl fluorides.

item.title: Allylation of (Hetero)aryl Thioethers and Related Compounds With 2‐Alkenylaziridines
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The allylation reaction of (hetero)aryl thioethers, aryl selenoethers, benzo[b]thiophenes, and dibenzo[b,d]thiophene is presented. The reaction exhibits high regioselectivity and mono- and bis-allylation controllability.


We report a transition-metal-free, atom-economical, and highly selective aryl allylation method of (hetero)aryl thioethers and aryl selenoethers with 2-alkenylaziridines in 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) under mild conditions. Adjusting the reactant ratio and reaction temperature enables selective access to either ortho-allylated or 2,6-bis-allylated aryl thioethers and aryl selenoethers. Benzo[b]thiophenes and dibenzo[b,d]thiophene also undergo allylation under the same conditions. The method accommodates a broad range of substrates, tolerates diverse functional groups, and exhibits good regioselectivity and Z/E selectivity.

item.title: Ball‐Milling‐Enabled Solvent‐ and Ligand‐Free Tsuji–Trost Reaction of C‐, N‐, O‐, S‐, and Se‐Nucleophiles in Air: Synthesis and Late‐Stage Modification of Drugs
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

This study reports the first ball-milling-enabled, ligand-free Tsuji–Trost reaction with allyl and cinnamyl acetates as well as allyl phosphate for the allylation of C-, N-, O-, S-, and Se-nucleophiles at room temperature under air without the need for a solvent. Thiophenols and benzeneselenol have been demonstrated for the first instance as nucleophiles in a ball-milling-assisted Tsuji–Trost reaction. In addition, this study successfully establishes the unexplored mechanochemical synthesis of a series of commercially available drugs containing allyl functional groups, as well as the late-stage modification of several marketed drugs.


We report a novel ball-milling-enabled, ligand-free Tsuji–Trost reaction involving C-, N-, O-, S-, and Se-nucleophiles with allyl and cinnamyl acetates, as well as allyl phosphate. Thiophenols and benzeneselenol have been demonstrated for the first time as nucleophiles in a ball-milling-assisted Tsuji–Trost reaction. The reaction proceeds at room temperature under air without the need for a solvent, and exhibits a broad substrate scope (41 examples). In addition, this study successfully establishes the unexplored mechanochemical synthesis of a series of commercially available drugs containing allyl functional groups, as well as the late-stage modification of several marketed drugs, highlighting the potential of this method in pharmaceutical applications and drug discovery. The practical utility of this methodology is further demonstrated through a gram-scale reaction of the Cinnarizine drug, followed by downstream derivatization and reusability of the catalyst. Additionally, several spectroscopic experiments have been conducted for the first time to gain mechanistic insight and elucidate the proposed catalytic cycle of the Tsuji–Trost reaction under ball-milling conditions.

item.title: Sulfide‐Ene Reactions by Visible‐Light‐Mediated Phosphine Redox Catalysis
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A novel visible-light-mediated sulﬁde-ene reaction by phosphine redox catalysis is discovered, which enables regioselective incorporation of sulﬁde into highly complex substrates and drug derivatives, as well as application in bioconjugation and drug synthesis. This challenge is addressed by the mechanism of photoexcited P(III)–P(V) cation-catalyzed thiyl radical addition to alkenes.


Sulfur-containing compounds play a crucial role in many biological processes. The important gasotransmitter hydrogen sulfide (H2S) can be metabolized by cellular enzyme system for the biosynthesis of amino acids and regulatory effects related to diseases. Although the photocatalytic thiol-ene reactions have been widely developed, a general H2S-ene reaction by organic photocatalysis remains elusive. Inspired by enzyme-catalyzed SN2 dialkylation, we report a visible-light-mediated H2S-ene radical dialkylation by phosphine redox catalysis. This challenge is addressed by the mechanism of photoexcited P(III)–P(V) cation-catalyzed thiyl radical addition to alkenes. The H2S can be readily incorporated into a wide range of alkenes to access complex high-value-added sulfur-containing scaffolds, especially the late-stage functionalization of the alkenes derived from drugs and the cascade cyclization of dienes. This mild method also performs very well in the thiol-ene reactions, which are further applied to the synthesis of unsymmetric thioethers, macrocyclic sulfides, the conjugation of biomolecules, and sulfur-containing drugs. This strategy holds significant promise in the bioconjugation and the discovery of bioactive organosulfur compounds.

item.title: Detection of Hydrogen Spillover Over Pt Catalysts Supported on UiO‐66‐NO2 Under Practical Conditions and the Corresponding Ligand Effect
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The nitro groups in Pt/UiO-66-NO2 were substantially reduced to amino groups under 1.0 MPa H2 above 270 °C. Combined with the results of infrared measurements and hydrogenation reactions, this observation not only provides an evidence for the existence of hydrogen spillover in Pt/UiO-66-NO2 under practical conditions but also demonstrates that high temperature is needed for it to occur.


The existence and the roles of hydrogen spillover in heterogeneous catalysts under practical conditions are still under debate. This is particularly true for metal catalysts supported on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). Here, we prepared a Pt/UiO-66-NO2 catalyst and a Pt/UiO-66-NH2 catalyst by an impregnation method. The Pt particles were mainly on the external surface of UiO-66-NO2 and UiO-66-NH2, which excludes the atomic-scale intimacy between the functional groups and most of the Pt particles. We observed that the nitro groups in Pt/UiO-66-NO2 were substantially reduced to amino groups above 270 °C under 1.0 MPa H2. Since the reduction of aromatic nitro compounds over the Pt catalysts is easy to occur, the observation not only provides an evidence for the existence of hydrogen spillover in the metal catalysts supported on the UiO-66-type MOFs under practical conditions but also demonstrates that the occurrence of hydrogen spillover in the catalysts requires high temperature. The Pt/UiO-66-NO2 and Pt/UiO-66-NH2 catalysts reduced at 300 °C behaved similarly in several hydrogenation reactions, which differed from that of the Pt/UiO-66-NO2 catalysts reduced at 200 °C. Hence, we propose an indirect ligand effect of spillover hydrogen. It affects the catalytic performances of supported metal catalysts by affecting the functional groups of the supports.

item.title: Visible‐Light Cobalt‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Aroyl Amides From Arylazo Sulfones
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Blue Light and Cobalt Catalysis for Synthesis! A versatile strategy that combines photoactive arylazo sulfones as substrates and Co2(CO)8 as a catalyst for the preparation of aromatic amides is presented herein.


A versatile strategy leveraging the peculiar reactivity of arylazo sulfones as substrates bearing dyedauxiliary groups in arylation processes, combined with the catalytic activity of Co2(CO)8 in carbonylation reactions, enabled the efficient synthesis of aromatic amides. The present approach was successfully applied to the preparation of a library of aroyl amides (33 examples), showing broad functional-group tolerance. The desired products were obtained in discrete to excellent yields (42%–99%) under photocatalyst-free conditions through a robust, simple, and rapid protocol that takes advantage of relatively low CO pressures (10 bar).

item.title: A Structure‐Guided Multistrategy Design Enhances Thermostability of an α‐L‐Rhamnosidase for Efficient Biotransformation
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A structure-guided multiplatform rational design strategy was developed to enhance the thermostability of an α-L-rhamnosidase for industrial applications. The T384P mutant showed improved thermal stability, with a 4.4-fold increase in half-life at 65 °C and a 4.3 °C increase in melting temperature. It enabled efficient conversion of rutin to isoquercitrin at elevated temperatures, supporting its industrial potential.


α-L-Rhamnosidase is a key biocatalyst for natural product biotransformation, but its poor thermostability limits industrial applications. To address this challenge, this study developed a structure-guided multiplatform rational design strategy and applied it to a Bifidobacterium α-L-rhamnosidase (BcRha), identifying T384P as a key thermostable mutant. T384P exhibited a half-life of 353.3 min at 60 °C (3.3-fold that of the wild type, WT) and 81.8 min at 65 °C (4.4-fold), together with a 4.3 °C increase in melting temperature. Mechanistic analyses indicated that T384P enhanced thermostability by strengthening long-range dynamic coupling, establishing a multipoint polar locking network, and reducing global conformational fluctuations. Notably, combination mutants failed to exhibit synergistic enhancement, possibly due to coupling interference between distinct dynamic modules. Under high substrate loading (30 g/L rutin), T384P achieved an 18.8% higher isoquercitrin yield than WT at 60 °C and retained substantial activity at 65 °C, approximately twice that of WT. This study provides an efficient rational design strategy for improving α-L-rhamnosidase thermostability, reveals a possible mechanistic basis for nonadditive mutation effects, and offers a promising biocatalyst for high-temperature flavonoid biotransformation.

item.title: Site‐Selective Phosphonation of Arenes via Hypervalent Iodine‐Mediated C─H Functionalization
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A white light-promoted, metal-free strategy was developed for synthesizing structurally diverse aryl phosphonates via hypervalent iodine-mediated C─H functionalization of arenes.


A white light-promoted, metal-free strategy based on hypervalent iodine-mediated C─H functionalization was developed for the synthesis of aryl phosphonates. This method facilitates the straightforward conversion of an array of arenes into their respective diaryliodonium salts, which are subsequently subjected to a metal-free phosphonation process to yield structurally diverse aryl phosphonates. Furthermore, the practical synthetic value of this approach was demonstrated through its application in the late-stage structural diversification of complex molecules.

item.title: Front Cover: Aromaticity‐Driven Photochemistry With Thioamide Platforms for Dual‐Mode Cross‐Electrophile Coupling (Adv. Synth. Catal. 20/2026)
item.description:

Metal-free Photocatalysis

Light, aromaticity, and no metals: pro-aromatic thioamides acting as photoauxiliaries, forming photoactive electron donor–acceptor complexes in the presence of sacrificial reductants, and as organic photocatalysts, whose excited states undergo reductive quenching, to forge C−C bonds through visible-light cross-electrophile coupling. This dual-mode, precious-metal-free platform delivers bioactive phenolic scaffolds with promising antimicrobial activity against clinically relevant pathogens. More in the Research Article (10.1002/adsc.70763), A. Jean-Luc Ayitou and co-workers.

item.title: Sequential Catalysis Enables C2‐Preferential Functionalization of Quinone Imine Ketal With α‐Amino Ynones
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A sequential catalytic system was developed for the regioselective coupling of quinone imine ketal 2 with pyrrolone nucleophiles generated in situ from racemic α-amino ynones 1. This protocol combines Au-catalyzed nucleophile formation with CuCl/rac-CPA-promoted regioselective trapping, affording C2-addition products 3 in moderate to good yields. Representative C3-addition products 4 obtained under CPA-controlled conditions further reveal the tunable regioselectivity of this system.


A sequential AuCl/CuCl/CPA catalytic system was developed for the C2-preferential coupling of QIK 2a with pyrrolone nucleophiles generated in situ from α-amino ynones. This protocol combines Au-catalyzed nucleophile formation with CuCl/rac-CPA-promoted regioselective trapping, affording C2-addition products in moderate to good yields. Representative C3-addition products obtained under CPA-controlled conditions further reveal the tunable regioselectivity of this system. Preliminary asymmetric studies with enantiopure CPAs delivered selected C2 adducts with up to 82% ee , and scale-up/derivatization experiments demonstrated the synthetic utility of the products.

item.title: Cover Feature: Photoredox/Pyridine N‐Oxide Catalyzed Acyl Radical Generation From Aldehydes for Divergent Synthesis of Pyrroles and Carbocyclic Ketones (Adv. Synth. Catal. 20/2026)
item.description:

Hydrogen-Atom Transfer

Under blue light, photoredox catalysis and pyridine N-oxide-mediated hydrogen-atom transfer convert readily available aldehydes into acyl radicals. Addition of these radicals to alkynes opens three aldehyde-dependent pathways to densely functionalized pyrroles, cyclopentanones, or indanones. The cover illustrates this divergent catalytic platform, which transforms simple feedstocks into valuable heterocyclic and carbocyclic molecular scaffolds. More in the Research Article (10.1002/adsc.70748), Yongming Deng and co-workers.

item.title: Selective Electroreductive N‐Alkylation of Nitroarenes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

We report an electrocatalytic reductive coupling of nitroarenes with alkyl halides that enables the direct and step-economic synthesis of N-alkylarylamines. This protocol features mild electrochemical conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and an exceptionally wide substrate scope, accommodating both benzylic and aliphatic halides.


Aryl amines are privileged structural motifs ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and natural products. Herein, we report an electrocatalytic reductive coupling of nitroarenes with alkyl halides that enables the direct and step-economic synthesis of N-alkylarylamines. This protocol features mild electrochemical conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and an exceptionally wide substrate scope, accommodating both benzylic and aliphatic halides. The synthetic utility of this method is further underscored by gram-scale synthesis and a series of downstream derivatizations, highlighting its practicality and sustainability.

item.title: Cobalt‐Catalyzed B─H Alkenylation of 1,2‐Azaborines With Terminal Alkynes
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

The development of general and efficient strategies for direct transformation of B─H bonds in 1,2-azaborines remains scarce and challenging. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed B─H alkenylation reaction of 1,2-azaborines with terminal alkynes. The method provides a versatile platform for the atom-economic construction of diverse alkenyl-substituted 1,2-azaborines in high yields, with excellent regio- and stereoselectivities. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad substrate scope, and excellent functional group tolerance.

Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed B─H alkenylation reaction of 1,2-azaborines with terminal alkynes. The method provides a versatile platform for the atom-economic construction of diverse alkenyl-substituted 1,2-azaborines in high yields, with excellent regio- and stereoselectivities. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad substrate scope, and excellent functional group tolerance.

item.title: Advances in Transition‐Metal‐Catalyzed 1,2‐N‐Migrations via Carbon‐Centered Carbenes and Radicals
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Described herein is a summary of present research on the 1,2-N-migrations onto metal carbene centers and carbon radical centers. This strategy provides a convenient and highly attractive way for the construction of structurally complex nitrogen-containing molecules and diverse nitrogen heterocycles.


1,2-N-migrations onto metal carbenes and carbon radicals have been substantially applied as a guiding strategy in structurally complex nitrogen-containing molecules and diverse nitrogen heterocycles. This strategy can construct structural complexity through a molecular skeletal recombination due to the fact that this type of reaction involves the carbon–nitrogen bond cleavage and formation between three adjacent atoms. In recent years, the field of 1,2-N-migrations onto metal carbenes and carbon radicals has experienced rapid development and a range of efficient synthetic protocols have been documented. In this review, we will focus on the recent progress in the 1,2-N-migrations onto metal carbenes as well as carbon radicals and the mechanistic research is showcased where possible.

item.title: Beyond Wittig: Phosphonium Ylides and Salts as Catalysts and Precursors in Radical Chemistry
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Phosphonium ylides and salts go beyond Wittig chemistry to act as catalysts and radical precursors, generating carbon- and phosphorus-centered radicals via P–C homolysis, photoinduced SET, and HAT. This review discusses the mechanisms, limitations, and future opportunities of these single-electron transformations.


Phosphonium ylides are classically recognized as nucleophilic reagents for carbonyl olefination. However, recent studies have revealed that their reactivity extends well beyond conventional two-electron processes. They serve as catalysts in radical reactions and as sources of carbon-centered radicals under thermal or photochemical activation. We give particular attention to the mechanistic distinctions among direct P─C bond homolysis, photoinduced single-electron transfer (SET), and ylide radical-cation-mediated hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT). Structurally related phosphonium salts are discussed separately as complementary radical precursors that undergo single-electron activation and selective P─C bond fragmentation to generate carbon- or phosphorus-centered radicals. The review also evaluates the experimental evidence used to support these mechanisms and identifies current limitations in substrate scope and catalytic efficiency. Future opportunities in catalyst design, asymmetric synthesis, electrochemical activation, and flow photochemistry are also outlined. These developments broaden the established reactivity profile of organophosphorus compounds and provide a foundation for more general and predictive single-electron transformations.

item.title: Atroposelective Synthesis of Axially Chiral Diaryl Ethers via Organocatalyzed Enantioselective Desymmetric Allyl Addition
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed allylation of prochiral dialdehydes with allylboronate provides C─O axially chiral diaryl ethers with simultaneous control of C─O axial and benzylic central chirality. The retained aldehyde group enables versatile downstream transformations.


Catalytic asymmetric construction of C─O axially chiral diaryl ethers remains underdeveloped relative to C─C biaryl atropisomers, and examples that simultaneously create a stereogenic carbon center are scarce. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed enantioselective allyl addition of prochiral dialdehydes with allylboronate, which enables the efficient synthesis of a novel class of axially chiral diaryl ethers bearing both C─O axial chirality and a stereogenic benzylic carbon center. This protocol provides the desired products in good diastereoselectivities and enantioselectivities under mild conditions. The retained aldehyde group serves as a versatile handle for diverse downstream transformations, substantially enhancing the structural and functional diversity of the atropisomeric scaffolds.

item.title: Modular Photocatalytic Three‐Component Gem‐Difluoroalkylative Pyridylation of Alkenes via Pyridylphosphonium Salts
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Reported herein is a photocatalytic protocol for the gem-difluoroalkylative pyridylation of alkenes using pyridylphosphonium salts and gem-difluoroalkyl reagents. The method tolerates diverse alkenes and, via 1,5-HAT, extends to unactivated ones, broadening the scope of alkene difunctionalization while also offering a promising new strategy for the diverse modification of complex pharmaceuticals.


The difunctionalization of alkenes enables the efficient and simultaneous construction of two chemical bonds. However, methods for the simultaneous introduction of both a pyridine ring and a difluoromethyl group into alkene molecules remain scarce. Here, we report a strategy for the gem-difluoroalkylative pyridylation of alkenes under mild conditions using pyridylphosphonium salts as pyridine unit donors. This reaction enables highly regioselective installation of a pyridine unit and a gem-difluoromethyl group across the C═C bond, featuring broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance. Furthermore, this protocol can be extended to enable remote C(sp3)─H bond functionalization via a 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer, providing a route for rapid construction of molecular complexity and late-stage derivatization of complex fluorinated molecules.

item.title: An Immobilized Marine Glycosyltransferase Acts as a Stabilized Biocatalyst for the Synthesis of Mannosylated Phosphoisoprenoids
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Mannosylated phosphoisoprenoids are generated by an immobilised glycosyltransferase as a sustainable approach towards the functionalisation of complex molecules.


Glycosylated phosphoisoprenoids constitute valuable bioactive molecules and starting materials for complex glycosylation cascades. Herein we report the identification and the functional characterization of a newly identified polyprenyl phosphomannose synthase from the marine microorganism Rhodococcus erythropolis PR4. This enzyme, normally unstable in its free form, is significantly stabilized by immobilization and can be reused up to four times for sustainable phosphoisoprenoid derivatization.

item.title: CS2 Induced Annulation of 2‐Alkynyl Nitroarenes With Indoles: Construction of 2,2‐Disubstituted Indolin‐3‐ones
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

An efficient, one-step synthesis of 2,2-disubstituted indolin-3-ones via a CS2-induced annulation between 2-alkynyl nitroarenes and indoles has been developed.


An efficient CS2 induced annulation of 2-alkynyl nitroarenes with indoles for the construction of 2,2-disubstituted indolin-3-ones has been developed. A range of functionalized indolin-3-ones were prepared in moderate to good yields from easily available starting materials. This reaction directly synthesizes 2,2-disubstituted indol-3-ones from ortho-alkynyl nitroarenes in a single step. This protocol avoids the need for preformed isatogen intermediates that require noble transition metal catalysis in prior methods.

item.title: Dual Regulation of Interfacial OH− Enrichment and d‍‐‍Orbital Engineering in S‐Doped Ni(OH)2 for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Methanol Oxidation to Formate
item.description: The electrocatalytic methanol (MeOH) selective oxidation reaction (MSOR) offers a promising strategy for H2 production and value-added chemical synthesis, yet its efficiency is often limited by insufficient interfacial OH− supply and competing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at Ni-based electrocatalysts. Herein, we demonstrate that S incorporation into nickel hydroxide (Ni(OH)S) simultaneously regulates the interfacial reaction environment and the electronic structure of Ni active sites, thereby accelerating the turnover of NiOOH during MeOH electrooxidation. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal that S doping strengthens interfacial OH− enrichment, which facilitates the rapid electrochemical reconstruction of Ni(OH)2 into NiOOH under anodic polarization. More importantly, the modified dx2−y2$d_{{x^{2}}-{y^{2}}}$ electronic configuration promotes the subsequent chemical reaction between NiOOH and MeOH, preventing excessive NiOOH accumulation and suppressing the competing OER. The resulting Ni(OH)S electrocatalyst achieves 100 mA·cm−2 at only 1.40 V and maintains >90 % Faradaic efficiency of formate over a broad potential window (1.40–1.80 V) with long-term stability exceeding 60 h. This work demonstrates an effective strategy to simultaneously enhance interfacial OH− availability and mitigate competitive OER in Ni-based MSOR electrocatalysts.

item.title: Recent Advances in Triplet Free‐Carbene Transfer Chemistry
item.description: Photoinduced free-carbene transfer reactions have emerged as a powerful and practical method for enabling a wide range of C─C and C─X bond-forming transformations and synthesizing structurally diverse and complex molecules. However, the spin state of free-carbene intermediates is a crucial parameter for understanding their chemical properties and reactivity. Selective generation of triplet free-carbene intermediates, which feature diradical character, is challenging but highly desirable. Such protocols are intriguing for developing novel synthetic methods and achieving unprecedented selectivity. Over the past 5 years, the development of photocatalysis has unlocked the capability of triplet carbene intermediates in synthetic applications. In this review article, we categorize these recent advancements into four classes, including (a) [3 + 2]-cyclization with alkynes, (b) stepwise addition with alkenes, (c) C─C bond insertion with BCBs, and (d) C─H/X─H/C─X bond insertion and coupling reactions. The discussion focuses on the catalytic generation of triplet carbene species, reaction design, mechanistic pathways, and substrate scope. We aim to present a unified perspective on the current state-of-the-art in triplet free-carbene chemistry under light-driven conditions, while also highlighting future research opportunities in this emerging field.

item.title: Sequential Hydrogen Atom Transfer‐Mediated Electrochemical Diselenylation of Oxindoles to Access Antifungal gem‐Diselenides
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

A sustainable and efficient electrochemical strategy was developed for the direct C(sp³)–H gem-diselenylation of oxindoles through a dual hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) pathway. The resulting gem-diselenides exhibit broad-spectrum inhibitory activity against diverse phytopathogens, highlighting their potential as lead compounds for further development.


Herein, we report a sustainable and efficient electrochemical strategy for the direct C(sp3)─H gem-diselenylation of oxindoles. This protocol proceeds under oxidant- and metal-free conditions, exploiting the synergistic interplay between electrochemical activation and iodide mediation to drive the transformation. This method demonstrates practical utility through a broad substrate scope, gram-scale synthesis, and late-stage functionalization of drug molecules. Mechanistic investigations reveal that iodide ions are pivotal, with evidence supporting a radical pathway. Finally, the synthesized gem-diselenide products exhibit good inhibitory activity against a variety of plant pathogens and can be identified as promising lead compounds for further exploration.

item.title: Semireduction of Secondary Aryl Amides to Imines Using a Mixed Aluminum Hydride Reagent
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Aryl amides can be selectively reduced to imines using a combination of aluminum hydride reagents.


Aryl amides and imines are among the most commonly encountered functional groups in synthetic organic chemistry, appearing in numerous biologically active pharmaceuticals and natural products.
